title: Sunkapogue Creek (Mastic Neck)
summary: Sunkapogue is a creek in Brookhaven on Mastic Neck, connected with the east bounds of a half-neck of land.
history_content: The creek appears in an April 1, 1690 deed from Macarac, also known as Humphrey, an Unkechaug person, to Andrew Gibb. The modern marker is a general Mastic Neck creek placement.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Sunkapogue and Sunkapauk. The name is interpreted as cool water-place, or a spring or brook of running water.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names are more than a name, they contain stories, and are Indigenous Knowledge and may not be shared with you.”

— Signal Fire: Natural Science and Reconciliation in Canada, Call 6: Uplift Indigenous Place Names (n.d.), Call 6 introduction
preservation_content: Sunkapogue adds another creek name to the Unkechaug and Mastic Neck record landscape, where watercourses shaped deed boundaries and remembered places.
